limit_order_match_processing.meaning: a limit order match (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_processing.checkpoint: before the limit order match validation

matched_base_amount.meaning: matched base amount of the limit order match
matched_base_amount.checkpoint: before the limit order match validation

matched_quote_amount.meaning: matched quote amount of the limit order match
matched_quote_amount.checkpoint: before the limit order match validation

matched_amounts_bitwise_and.meaning: bitwise AND of matched base amount and matched quote amount (zero iff no overlapping 1-bits)
matched_amounts_bitwise_and.checkpoint: derived from matched amounts before the limit order match validation

base_amount_nonzero.checkpoint: before the limit order match validation

quote_amount_nonzero.checkpoint: before the limit order match validation

zero_cost_trade_revert_occurred.meaning: the limit order match reverted with ZeroCostTrade()
zero_cost_trade_revert_occurred.checkpoint: at limit order match execution outcome

assumptions: The matched base and quote amounts are observable prior to the ZeroCostTrade() validation.
The disjoint-bit condition is treated as a potential scenario configuration, not an observed prior state.

unresolved.description: The report states 'no overlapping 1-bits' only qualitatively with an example (base = 256, quote in {1..255}); the bitwise-AND-zero relation is encoded via a derived product placeholder because the grammar has no bitwise operator, so the exact bitwise relation is not faithfully expressible.

limitations: The bitwise disjointness is approximated by a derived symbol; the grammar lacks a bitwise AND operator.
Caller identity/authorization is not part of the selected P/I/V and is not encoded.
Fill-order validation logic is out of scope for this claim.
